fund-js/08-strings-and-regular-expressio.instructions:
**Skills:** normalize · regular expressions  
**Level:** ★★☆

**Interview prompt.** "Product URLs are built from titles. 'Crème Brûlée  — 2 for 1!' must become a clean slug, and a 300-character title must not produce a 300-character URL."

**Why it matters.** Slugs combine Unicode normalisation (strip accents), character classes (keep letters and digits), collapsing runs, and careful trimming. Each step is a one-line regex, and getting their order wrong produces double dashes and trailing junk.

**Your task.** Export `slugify(title, maxLength)` (`maxLength` defaults to 60):
- remove accents (decompose with NFD and drop the combining marks)
- lowercase
- every run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits becomes a single `-`
- no leading or trailing `-`
- the result is at most `maxLength` characters; if cutting leaves a trailing `-`, remove it
- a title with no letters or digits gives the empty string

**Worked example.** `slugify('Crème Brûlée  — 2 for 1!')` is `'creme-brulee-2-for-1'`.
hints: Removing accents only works after normalize has split each accented letter into a base letter and a separate mark.
Decompose accented letters first and remove the separate marks, then lower-case, collapse every run of other characters into one dash, trim dashes from both ends, and cut to length last.
Decompose the letters, delete the accent marks, lowercase, turn every stretch of other characters into a single dash, trim dashes at both ends, then shorten and trim the end once more.
